title: Private: SSO role-propagation edge case causing cross-tenant elevation — urgent patch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers on Private clusters reported that users with tenant-scoped SAML assertions occasionally received elevated tenant roles (cross-tenant admin role) during high request rates. This is reproducible when the identity gateway receives concurrent SAML assertions containing multiple role claims with inconsistent scoping attributes. The symptom surface: audit logs show role assignment events without a matching scoped role claim; KMS envelope metadata for the role assignment operation is missing in some audit entries. This ticket tracks diagnosis, patch, and rollout of an urgent fix for the role propagation race and missing KMS metadata in Private control planes.
repro_steps: Deploy Private control plane with Okta/Azure SAML integration and tenant-bound role mapping rules
Create two role claims in IdP assertion: one scoped to tenant A (tenant_id claim), one generic role claim without tenant scope
Simulate 200 concurrent SSO logins targeting the same service node (use load-test harness: tests/sso/multi-claim-load.py)
Observe in auth logs: intermittent role assigned as global-admin to sessions that should have tenant-scoped roles
Check audit log entries for assign_role events — some entries are missing 'kms_key_id' in envelope metadata
impact: Customers on Private deployments may see temporary privilege escalation for a subset of SSO logins and incomplete audit trails for those events. Business impact: potential data exposure across tenant boundaries and failure to meet audit/compliance controls until patch is deployed.
root_cause: Race condition in identity-gatekeeper worker: attribute extraction and tenant normalization run in parallel with RBAC mapping when assertions contain multiple role claims. When normalization loses the scoped attribute due to non-atomic updates, the RBAC engine defaults to an unscoped role mapping. Additionally, a separate code path that enriches audit events with KMS envelope metadata is skipped when the fast-path RBAC cache returns a value before metadata is attached.
proposed_fix:
1) Make SAML attribute extraction and tenant normalization atomic for a single assertion processing flow (single-threaded per-assertion or use a processing lock)
2) Harden RBAC mapping to validate presence of tenant-scoped attributes before applying unscoped role rules
3) Ensure KMS envelope metadata attach is done synchronously before RBAC commit to audit log, and add a defensive fallback that inserts placeholder key IDs if enrichment fails
4) Add unit/integration tests that reproduce the multi-claim concurrent path and verify audit metadata presence
rollout_plan: Smoke deploy to internal canary Private cluster (canary-priv-1) with synthetic high-rate SSO load
Stage rollout to a subset of customers in 2 waves (10% then 50%) with feature-gate 'enforce-atomic-assertion' off by default
If metrics are stable for 24h, flip feature-gate on globally and schedule controlled restart of control-plane nodes
Coordinate with Support to notify impacted customers and offer immediate mitigations
qa_checks: Automated regression: run tests/sso/multi-claim-load.py under 10k concurrent requests with assertions that previously triggered the bug
Verify audit logs for all assign_role events include 'kms_key_id' and 'assertion_id' fields
Run static analysis for potential deadlocks introduced by processing lock
Manual verification with 3 customers' staging clusters (contacts in attachments)
monitoring_signals: increase in assign_role error rate (Sentry alert rule: RBAC-Assign-Err > 1/min)
auth latency spike on identity-gatekeeper (< 5% degradation acceptable)
customer_communications: Initial advisory (March 10): private customers with SAML told about investigation (ticket reference ENG-23670)
Mitigation email (March 12): suggested short-term workaround: disable unscoped role mapping in tenant policy; instructions linked in attachments
Patch announcement (post-rollout): security bulletin with CVSS-like impact, change log, and guidance to verify audit logs
